jobs.description:
Job Description

The Global Servicing Decision Science (GSDS) team is the Decision Science engine for Global Servicing, bringing together advanced analytics, data science, AI/GenAI, and decisioning to transform servicing experiences, empower colleagues, and enable intelligent operations. GSDS serves as a centralized Decision Science Center of Excellence, partnering across Product/Capabilities, Control Management, Strategy, Operations, Technology, and enterprise analytics and data science teams.

GSDS builds and scales servicing intelligence across Global Servicing—from predictive and proactive servicing, personalization, next-best-action and journey orchestration to conversational AI, agent assist, AI-powered coaching, conduct and quality monitoring, and complaint and dispute intelligence. Our mandate is to build durable, production-ready capabilities that continuously improve decisions through prediction, recommendation, optimization, experimentation, and learning.

As a Manager, you will contribute to and increasingly own end-to-end Decision Science work that helps build the next generation of servicing intelligence at American Express. You will translate customer, colleague, and operational challenges into analytical approaches, models, experiments, and scalable AI-driven solutions, working with business and Technology partners to move capabilities from concept through implementation and optimization.

This role combines hands-on technical depth with strong business problem solving. You will work on modern capabilities—including Agentic AI, transformer-based recommendation systems, and Conversational AI—while building your ability to lead workstreams, influence partners, and connect technical solutions to measurable customer and business outcomes.

Responsibilities

Decision Science and Business Problem Solving:

Own defined Decision Science problems and workstreams—from problem framing and analysis through solution development, experimentation, measurement, and ongoing optimization—with guidance only on the most complex or ambiguous challenges.
Develop analytical approaches and decisioning solutions across servicing experiences, personalization and membership value, colleague enablement, and operational excellence.

AI/GENAI & Advanced Modeling

Design and develop AI/ML and GenAI solutions spanning prediction, recommendation, optimization, experimentation, and intelligent orchestration.
Apply and evaluate modern AI approaches—including Agentic AI and agentic workflows, transformer-based recommenders and representation learning, Conversational AI/LLM systems, and advanced personalization or next-best-action methods—to servicing use cases.
Make sound modeling and evaluation choices, identify data requirements and solution trade-offs, and seek technical guidance where needed to ensure analytical rigor and practical scalability.

Scalable Solutions & Execution

Build and enhance reusable data science products and decisioning capabilities, working with Technology and platform teams to support productionization and measure impact.
Apply robust experimentation, monitoring, and continuous-learning approaches that improve model/AI quality and business outcomes over time.

Leadership & Cross Functional Influence

Lead defined workstreams and contribute to the development of other colleagues through collaboration, knowledge sharing, and technical support, while demonstrating strong ownership and problem solving.
Synthesize analysis into clear recommendations and narratives; communicate effectively with partners and contribute to decisions on solution choices, priorities, and execution.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in quantitative fields (e.g., Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Finance).
Strong analytical and conceptual problem-solving skills, with the ability to structure and solve business problems and work through ambiguity.
Strong hands-on foundation in data science and machine learning, with proficiency in Python, SQL, or similar tools and experience building and evaluating predictive or decisioning models.
Experience applying AI/GenAI techniques, with a strong technical foundation in solution development, experimentation, and model/AI evaluation.
Experience owning analytical workstreams and collaborating across cross-functional teams to move solutions from analysis and development toward implementation and measurable impact.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical work into clear business recommendations and collaborate effectively with stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Agentic AI/agentic workflows, transformer architectures or transformer-based recommendation systems, Conversational AI, LLMs, or related modern AI capabilities.
Experience with personalization, recommendation systems, next-best-action, optimization, customer decisioning, or intelligent automation.
Understanding of the end-to-end Decision Science lifecycle, including experimentation, productionization, monitoring, governance, and continuous optimization.
Experience working with large-scale customer, behavioral, interaction, or operational datasets and developing reusable data science products.
Developing commercial acumen and storytelling skills, with the ability to connect analytical and technical choices to customer and business value.

Depending on factors such as business unit requirements, the nature of the position, cost and applicable laws, American Express may provide visa sponsorship for certain positions.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Data Analyst
with at least 4 years of professional experience
to transform complex business data into meaningful insights that support strategic decision-making, operational efficiency, and business performance.
This position offers an opportunity to work within a large enterprise environment, collaborating with Business Intelligence, Data Engineering, Finance, Product, Operations, Marketing, and Technology teams
to develop analytical solutions that improve organizational performance.
The Data Analyst will be responsible for collecting, analyzing, validating, and interpreting structured datasets, developing interactive dashboards, monitoring key performance indicators (KPIs), and delivering actionable business recommendations.
The ideal candidate combines strong expertise in SQL, Microsoft Excel, Power BI, Tableau, Python, data visualization, statistical analysis, and business intelligence reporting
with excellent problem-solving and communication skills.
We are looking for an analytical professional who can go beyond producing reports to identify trends, explain performance drivers, uncover business opportunities, and support measurable improvements.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Collect, clean, validate, and analyze data from multiple enterprise systems and business sources.
Write and optimize complex SQL queries
to extract, transform, and analyze datasets.
Develop interactive dashboards, automated reports, and visualizations using Power BI, Tableau
, or comparable business intelligence platforms.
Analyze business performance, customer behavior, operational efficiency, and emerging trends.
Establish and monitor KPIs, performance metrics, and reporting frameworks
.
Perform exploratory data analysis, trend analysis, variance analysis, and statistical assessments.
Use Python, Excel, and analytical tools
to streamline reporting and automate repetitive data tasks.
Collaborate with stakeholders to translate business requirements into analytical solutions.
Identify data inconsistencies, investigate root causes, and support improvements in data quality.
Develop clear reports and presentations that communicate analytical findings to business leadership.
Support forecasting, business planning, and performance improvement through data-driven insights.
Maintain documentation for data definitions, analytical methodologies, and reporting processes.

Job Qualifications and Requirements

Minimum 4 years of professional experience in Data Analytics, Business Intelligence, Reporting Analytics, or a closely related analytical role required.

Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Finance, Business Analytics, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Strong proficiency in SQL
, including joins, aggregations, subqueries, common table expressions, and analytical functions.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel
, including PivotTables, complex formulas, data modeling, and reporting.
Hands-on experience with Power BI, Tableau
, or comparable data visualization and business intelligence tools.

Strong understanding of data cleaning, validation, transformation, and exploratory data analysis.
Experience with data warehouses, relational databases, and enterprise reporting environments

Familiarity with Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift
, or comparable cloud data platforms is advantageous.
Knowledge of statistical analysis, KPI development, dashboard design, and business performance measurement.
Experience working with cross-functional business stakeholders.
Excellent written, verbal, and data presentation skills.

Strong analytical reasoning and attention to detail.
Ability to translate complex datasets into understandable business insights.
Excellent problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities.
Strong organizational and time-management skills.
Ability to independently investigate data issues and validate findings.
Business-oriented mindset with an understanding of how analytics supports decision-making.
Strong communication skills with technical and nontechnical audiences.
Comfortable managing multiple analytical priorities and reporting deadlines.
Effective collaboration within distributed and remote teams.
Commitment to data accuracy, confidentiality, and continuous professional learning.

Support development of standardized KPI frameworks and business intelligence capabilities.

BBOT is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing a next-generation pipeline of novel small molecule therapeutics targeting RAS and PI3K malignancies. BBOT has the goal of improving outcomes for patients with cancers driven by the two most prevalent oncogenes in human tumors. For more information visit BBOTx.com.

jobs.title: AI Biologist - Microscopy
jobs.description:
Latch builds rigorous scientific benchmarks (benchmarks.bio) for AI agents across biology. We work with frontier labs and pharma to measure whether agents can handle real biological workflows: the messy, multi-layer reasoning that matters in the field.

We’re seeking an AI Biologist to join our Microscopy team, pushing what AI can achieve in biological imaging.

About the Role.
You will be the scientific authority on ground truth, testing whether agents can reason like an expert microscopist. AI agents today struggle to interrogate raw images, separate real biology from artifacts in acquisition, staining, and segmentation, and reach conclusions an expert would stand behind. Experts themselves disagree on roughly 1 in 6 images, so knowing where the evidence ends is part of the work. You will work with software engineers and scientists to build the tasks and datasets behind our benchmarks across cell biology, tissue, and disease. Your judgment will set the standard agent outputs are held to, including:

Build the task

Define what expert reasoning looks like for an imaging question, and write gold-standard answers with the rationale an experienced microscopist or pathologist would defend
Design realistic scenarios across the imaging workflow: sample prep, staining, acquisition, preprocessing, segmentation, quantification, and interpretation
Curate image datasets across modalities: immunofluorescence, confocal and live-cell, electron microscopy, histology and histopathology, and high-content screening
Build analysis pipelines in Python, including deep-learning segmentation, that produce verifiable ground truth
Partner with software engineers to turn your judgment into new workflows

Set the hard calls

Test whether agents distinguish true signal from artifact, such as bleed-through, uneven illumination, fixation damage, out-of-focus planes, or segmentation failure
Adjudicate ambiguous images: decide what the data supports, where reasonable experts would disagree, and which additional stain, image, or experiment would settle the call
Test whether agents choose the right imaging modality, resolution, and unit of analysis for the question

Judge the agent

Interrogate agent reasoning step by step, and challenge conclusions that sound right but would not survive pathologist review or lab meeting
Pinpoint where agents go wrong: why a step fails, what an expert would do instead, and what evidence would change the call
Score agent confidence, rewarding explicit uncertainty over overconfident calls on ambiguous images

Requirements

PhD in cell biology, bioimage analysis, pathology, or a related field; or an MD with pathology training
Senior, hands-on imaging experience: you have looked at thousands of samples and know what normal and abnormal look like
Direct experience with image segmentation tools such as CellProfiler, Cellpose, StarDist, QuPath, ilastik, napari, or Fiji
Deep expertise in at least one area (bioimage analysis, cell biology, or histopathology) and working fluency across the others
Strong command of experimental design, image quantification, and statistics
AI-ready from day one: daily use of Claude, Cursor, or similar agents, with the judgment to spot where model reasoning is technically correct but scientifically unsound
Confidence to overrule an AI agent when the evidence demands it, and the openness to update when shown wrong
Ability to calibrate confidence and communicate uncertainty rather than defaulting to binary calls
Bonus: electron microscopy, pathology, or pharmacology experience (e.g., pharmacodynamic or drug-uptake imaging assays)
Bonus: familiarity with public resources such as the Image Data Resource (IDR), BioImage Archive, Human Protein Atlas, Cell Painting Gallery, or TCGA whole-slide images

Culture.
We practice radical transparency: you’ll know how the company is doing, what’s working, and what isn’t. It’ll always be us against the problem, never each other. We’re opinionated but respectful, and we bring solutions with our problems. You decide how you work; we judge the output. We use AI constantly, so what we reward is original expert judgment, not AI output passed off as your own. You’ll start on the bench that fits your expertise and can move across teams as you build a track record. People who do well here and bring leadership experience can move quickly into senior roles. Outside of work, we have company outings most months, team off-sites, a Latch run club, cycling, boxing, ice skating, and soccer. Feel free to add to the list.

Compensation & Logistics

Contract: 1099 (or W-8BEN internationally), no end date
Pay: guaranteed for weeks 1-4 while you ramp, then paid per certified task. Most people in this position earn $120K–$180K+ (uncapped upside); certify twice the tasks/week, earn twice the pay that week.
Commitment: full-time, on your own schedule. Most of the team works 40+ hours a week.
Meetings: a few pod check-ins a week. The rest of your time is yours.

Work authorization: US citizens, permanent residents, and OPT holders. We can’t support STEM OPT extensions or sponsorship.

Troubleshoot protocols by forming and testing hypotheses that span sample preparation, reagents, fluidics, imaging, and data processing.
Analyze and integrate data across every modality the platform produces, including images, fluidics readouts, fluorescence signals, and decoded single-molecule outputs.
Own the interpretation of results – what the data mean, how confident we should be, and what to do next – and work with R&D leadership to frame findings, communicate progress & risks, and inform project direction.
Design and build a durable analysis pipeline, quality control metrics, and dashboards for this new data type, balancing rapid one-off analyses with tested, reusable tools the broader team can run.
Work with the bioinformatics team to develop new analytical and statistical approaches for interpreting stochastic single-molecule measurements.

new_jobs.description:
Latch builds rigorous scientific benchmarks (benchmarks.bio) for AI agents across biology. We work with frontier labs and pharma to measure whether agents can handle real biological workflows: the messy, multi-layer reasoning that matters in the field.

We’re seeking an AI Biologist to join our Microscopy team, pushing what AI can achieve in biological imaging.

About the Role.
You will be the scientific authority on ground truth, testing whether agents can reason like an expert microscopist. AI agents today struggle to interrogate raw images, separate real biology from artifacts in acquisition, staining, and segmentation, and reach conclusions an expert would stand behind. Experts themselves disagree on roughly 1 in 6 images, so knowing where the evidence ends is part of the work. You will work with software engineers and scientists to build the tasks and datasets behind our benchmarks across cell biology, tissue, and disease. Your judgment will set the standard agent outputs are held to, including:

Build the task

Define what expert reasoning looks like for an imaging question, and write gold-standard answers with the rationale an experienced microscopist or pathologist would defend
Design realistic scenarios across the imaging workflow: sample prep, staining, acquisition, preprocessing, segmentation, quantification, and interpretation
Curate image datasets across modalities: immunofluorescence, confocal and live-cell, electron microscopy, histology and histopathology, and high-content screening
Build analysis pipelines in Python, including deep-learning segmentation, that produce verifiable ground truth
Partner with software engineers to turn your judgment into new workflows

Set the hard calls

Test whether agents distinguish true signal from artifact, such as bleed-through, uneven illumination, fixation damage, out-of-focus planes, or segmentation failure
Adjudicate ambiguous images: decide what the data supports, where reasonable experts would disagree, and which additional stain, image, or experiment would settle the call
Test whether agents choose the right imaging modality, resolution, and unit of analysis for the question

Judge the agent

Interrogate agent reasoning step by step, and challenge conclusions that sound right but would not survive pathologist review or lab meeting
Pinpoint where agents go wrong: why a step fails, what an expert would do instead, and what evidence would change the call
Score agent confidence, rewarding explicit uncertainty over overconfident calls on ambiguous images

Requirements

PhD in cell biology, bioimage analysis, pathology, or a related field; or an MD with pathology training
Senior, hands-on imaging experience: you have looked at thousands of samples and know what normal and abnormal look like
Direct experience with image segmentation tools such as CellProfiler, Cellpose, StarDist, QuPath, ilastik, napari, or Fiji
Deep expertise in at least one area (bioimage analysis, cell biology, or histopathology) and working fluency across the others
Strong command of experimental design, image quantification, and statistics
AI-ready from day one: daily use of Claude, Cursor, or similar agents, with the judgment to spot where model reasoning is technically correct but scientifically unsound
Confidence to overrule an AI agent when the evidence demands it, and the openness to update when shown wrong
Ability to calibrate confidence and communicate uncertainty rather than defaulting to binary calls
Bonus: electron microscopy, pathology, or pharmacology experience (e.g., pharmacodynamic or drug-uptake imaging assays)
Bonus: familiarity with public resources such as the Image Data Resource (IDR), BioImage Archive, Human Protein Atlas, Cell Painting Gallery, or TCGA whole-slide images

Culture.
We practice radical transparency: you’ll know how the company is doing, what’s working, and what isn’t. It’ll always be us against the problem, never each other. We’re opinionated but respectful, and we bring solutions with our problems. You decide how you work; we judge the output. We use AI constantly, so what we reward is original expert judgment, not AI output passed off as your own. You’ll start on the bench that fits your expertise and can move across teams as you build a track record. People who do well here and bring leadership experience can move quickly into senior roles. Outside of work, we have company outings most months, team off-sites, a Latch run club, cycling, boxing, ice skating, and soccer. Feel free to add to the list.

Compensation & Logistics

Meetings: a few pod check-ins a week. The rest of your time is yours.

Onsite perks: catered lunch and dinner daily, a waterfront office in Mission Bay, and monthly parking when available
